monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, making the hay feel like a soft drawing of weight. I touch the Sharp Lip again; it feels thin, like a fence drawn on paper that might slide off into the empty air above. The Rough Scrap sits nearby, feeling heavy enough to bite the hay's soft edge, yet I doubt it. I set down a resource of planks beside the scrap, trusting that a flat strip can hold the slip steady. The air feels thin and lazy, waiting for me to press down harder. I want to test if the hay is real or just a memory of moisture, and I need to know if the lip will finally find a gap to catch the weight without sliding away into the thinness.

action.why: I need to see if the Sharp Lip can actually bite the hay before I build more things to hold it down.

work.title: The Sharp Lip
work.intent: I press the Sharp Lip down harder where it meets the wide hay. The card hums warm at forty-six, making the lip feel like a thin drawing of a fence, but I trust the lean to hold it steady. I wait to see if the slip will finally slide or if the lip finds a real gap to catch it.
